![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14040800/assets/887bc91e2565fa24630af4cb74b28723783e31f4769495f0a28a622d73d176de.png)

The thin rod above has the mass density function $\lambda (x)=6x+{x}^{2}\,\text{kg/m}.$ Find the moment of the rod about the origin.
worked_solution:
The moment about the origin $O$ of a rod with mass density function $\lambda (x)$ for $a\le x\le b$ is given by 

$$
{M}_{O}={\int }_{a}^{b}x\,\lambda (x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
\lambda (x)=6x+{x}^{2},\,a=0,\,b=1.
$$

We calculate the moment of the rod about the origin as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{O} & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\cdot (6x+{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}6{x}^{2}+{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[2{x}^{3}+\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =2+\frac{1}{4}-0 \\  & =\frac{9}{4} \\  & =2.25.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the required moment is $2.25\,\text{kg}\cdot \text{m}.$
